column4: Visit note | 2025-09-24 10:00 AM | Dr. Nazma Begum, Obstetrics and Gynecology | Patient: Mahmuda Bhuiyan, 26, female. Mrs. Bhuiyan presents for her first visit stating that she has missed work or classes because of severe discomfort, describing painful cramps during the first days of each period accompanied by nausea. She is a shopkeeper and mentions that her symptoms have become worse since taking a job with long standing hours in Sirajganj, with the pain often spreading to her lower back and thighs along with vomiting. She has no other chronic illnesses or relevant past history. On examination: pain score 6/10, BP 132/82 mmHg, pulse 92 bpm, weight 55 kg. Abdomen is soft without tenderness outside the menstrual cycle. Assessment: Primary dysmenorrhoea. Plan: lifestyle and self-care advice only, no medicine needed at this stage, and no new prescription was issued today. She was advised to use a hot water bottle, do light exercise, and keep a period diary. Follow-up in 3 months with the period diary.
